FACT A:
entity: India
attribute: GDP growth rate
value: 7.2 per cent
normalised value: 7.2 percent
period: FY25 (2024-04-01 to 2025-03-31)
estimate type: projection
measurement basis: not stated
attributed to: Reserve Bank of India
document: 02-delhivery-annual-report-fy24-excerpt.pdf; publisher: Delhivery Limited; published: 2024-04-01
page label: 33
evidence verified: True (normalized)
quote: "The Reserve Bank of India has projected India’s GDP to grow at 7.2%1 in FY25."

FACT B:
entity: India
attribute: GDP growth rate
value: 6.5 per cent
normalised value: 6.5 percent
period: FY2024/25 (2024-04-01 to 2025-03-31)
estimate type: actual
measurement basis: not stated
attributed to: the document itself
document: 03-imf-india-2025-article-iv-excerpt.pdf; publisher: International Monetary Fund; published: 2025-11-01
page label: A2: 1
evidence verified: True (normalized)
quote: "Following economic growth of 6.5 percent in FY2024/25, real GDP expanded by 7.8 percent in the first quarter of FY2025/26."

Rule-engine hypothesis: attributed figure differs from first-party

Decide the verdict.

request.system:
You compare two facts extracted from two documents and decide how they relate.

Verdicts:
- corroborates: same quantity, same period, same basis, compatible values (allow rounding).
- superseded: same quantity and period, but a later data vintage or a revision replaces the
  earlier value; name which fact is newer.
- context_explained: the values differ because the period, scope/basis, unit or attribution
  differs; name that dimension. This is not a contradiction.
- contradicts: same quantity, period, basis and unit carry incompatible values.
- unresolved: the evidence does not settle it; give your best hypothesis in the explanation.

Use only the fields and quotes provided. Keep the explanation under 60 words and cite the
distinguishing phrase from each quote.

response.explanation: Fact A is a projection by the Reserve Bank of India ("projected India's GDP to grow at 7.2%"), whereas Fact B is an actual/historical figure reported by the IMF ("Following economic growth of 6.5 percent"). The estimate types and sources differ for the same period.
